<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **70** documentable anchor(s).

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e65452e601b5e853b003b9e64a620d2d0b3a5d`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e65452e601b5e853b003b9e64a620d2d0b3a5d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2645b03014f22da6c2bdc5b5b8b381e1f9dd5bb7` — the merge of head `2c293d536b5456be875c5ef1ed4a55866888e4ef` into base `b6e65452e601b5e853b003b9e64a620d2d0b3a5d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2645b03014f22da6c2bdc5b5b8b381e1f9dd5bb7 && git checkout 2645b03014f22da6c2bdc5b5b8b381e1f9dd5bb7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b6e65452e601b5e853b003b9e64a620d2d0b3a5d 2c293d536b5456be875c5ef1ed4a55866888e4ef && git checkout -B drift-repro b6e65452e601b5e853b003b9e64a620d2d0b3a5d && git merge --no-ff 2c293d536b5456be875c5ef1ed4a55866888e4ef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e65452e601b5e853b003b9e64a620d2d0b3a5d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b6e65452e601b5e853b003b9e64a620d2d0b3a5d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `da697f3fbdcb493ccd58a482a1f946a0e1516156`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #30808 (body, triage, unblock, claim, claim amendment, os-dev-report), PR #31398 body and file list (10 files, +1076/−36), the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff (the runtime seed paths, `isWritablePackage`, the ci.yml dogfood job, the engine-double gate's ledger header) was read to judge the diff, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

**Gate verdicts on this head (check-runs).** Green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Check PR Size, Flag docs, Test UI, Plan Test Core shards, filter. **NOT MEASURED (in progress at review time):** Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates (the family that carries `check:engine-double-contract`), Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI. **Dogfood Regression Gate** reads success, but its three shards are `skipped`: ci.yml runs them only off `pull_request` (merge queue and main), so the new dogfood file is NOT MEASURED on this head in CI. Its only evidence is the dev's local run (3 files, 34 tests). It is measured when the PR enters the queue. This PASS judges the code. Landing still waits for every NOT MEASURED family above.

**(a) Is the widening limited to the door switch and the verb's in-process type, with no `packages/spec` change?** The spec half holds. No path under `packages/spec` is in the diff, and `ImportUnmanagedPackageRequestSchema` is untouched. `seedData` is destructured off before the strict parse, as `actor` is, and the strict parse still refuses an undeclared key (pinned by the `withSampleData` 400 case). `git grep` finds one caller of `importUnmanagedPackage`: the install-local door. No HTTP route hands a raw body to the verb, so `seedData` cannot be stated from outside. The door body is the plugin's own, and no spec schema describes it. The new helpers (`unmanagedSeedItems`, `UNMANAGED_SEED_TYPE`, `seedDatasetOfReceiptItem`) are not re-exported from either package index, so no export surface changes.
The accept-set half is not complete. The diff widens three things, and the declaration names two:
- `POST /marketplace/install-local` accepts `seedSampleData` (boolean, unmanaged only). Named right. The non-boolean and managed-install 400s are pinned and ablated.
- The verb's in-process request type gains `seedData`. Named right.
- `POST /marketplace/install-local/:id/purge-sample-data` is **not named** in either `Clause-②` line. Before, any id without an install-ledger entry answered 404. Now an id that names an installed writable base answers one of three things: 200, deleting the rows its active `seed` items name; 400 `NOTHING_TO_PURGE`; or 503. The branch's predicate is `registry.getPackage(id) && isWritablePackage(ql, id)`, and `isWritablePackage` is true for every project-scoped base, not only an unmanaged copy. So a Studio-authored base's own published `seed` items are now purgeable through this door. The changeset says the purge works "on a copy". The PR body says "an installed, writable base", which is closer but still does not name the reach. The classification `yes (widening)` stays right, and the tier is unchanged. The declaration is incomplete and the reach is wider than the card's ask. → should-fix S1.
- The unmanaged answer's `seeded` can now take `mode: 'inline'` or `'refused'`, and new `skipped` reasons (`no-datasets`, `seed-receipt-unread: …`, `seed-error: …`). This is door-local and is the shape the managed path already answers. Right.

**(b) Can storing the copy's seed items in the environment ledger make any boot, save or publish re-insert rows after a purge?**
- **Boot: no.** Code read: no boot path applies a `sys_metadata` `seed` item. The runtime's seed loaders read the config app's `data` (inline seed), the artifact's `metadata:reloaded` payload (hot reload), and the shared `seed-datasets` list (per-org replay). The unmanaged path never calls `applySideEffects`, so the copy is never merged into `seed-datasets`, and an org founded later does not replay it. The copy also writes no ledger entry, so the rehydrate healer never sees it. The dogfood pin is real. It counts rows across all five objects under a system context on one database file, in three boots: after install exactly 28; after restart 28 plus 1 user row; after purge 0 plus 1; after a second restart 0 plus 1, and the surviving name is `User Authored Co`. That is discriminating. One caveat: the counts are taken as soon as `bootShowcase` resolves, so a load that ran after boot returned would be missed. No such load exists in the code, so this does not affect the verdict. The cloud-connection restart pin re-mounts only the plugin over a protocol double, so it shows only that the plugin's own `kernel:ready` loads nothing. That is correct for a unit pin, and the dogfood file carries the real claim.
- **Save: no.** Code read: seed rows are applied only by `runPublishSideEffects` (`publishMetaItem`) and by `publishPackageDrafts`, never by `saveMetaItem`. The pin for this does not discriminate, though. The protocol case calls `saveMetaItem({ mode: 'publish' })` while rows `a1`/`a2` already exist, so an applied create-only seed would also insert 0, and the assertion would pass either way. → should-fix S2.
- **Publish: yes, and this is not stated.** The purge leaves the receipt (by design; the second-purge case pins it). A later draft and publish of a receipt item runs `applySeedBodies` create-only, so every purged row comes back. These rows are owned by the loader's D9 rule, not by the installer, because the publish path does no installer stamp. This is how any environment `seed` item behaves, and it needs an author's deliberate publish, so it is not a defect of this PR. But the changeset and PR body say a later publish "loads no row twice" without the after-purge case, and nothing pins it. → should-fix S3.

**(c) Are the seed rows owned by the installer, as ruled (#30324 C / #30680 A)?** Yes. `loadUnmanagedCopySeeds` runs the managed path's `runInlineSeed` with `owner: { userId, door: 'unmanaged install' }`, and `stampLoadOwner` / `stampSeedOwner` write `owner_id` and `created_by` on every row the load created. The diff adds no sample-data read rule, so the rows follow ordinary permissions. The copy's objects are new, so every loaded row is a created row, and a matched pre-existing row cannot keep a foreign owner. Pinned twice: the unit case checks `owner_id`/`created_by` equal `usr_installer` on every row, and the dogfood file checks that the owner set and the creator set across all 28 rows are both exactly the signed-in person's id. That id is taken from a row the same person wrote through REST. Ablation `userId: null` goes red. The card also asked the PR to state a consequence: per-role answers in the customer's environment will differ from the gallery's per-persona transcripts. The PR states the collapse to one owner, but not that consequence. → should-fix S4.

**Card asks.**
- Ask 1 (optional, off by default): pinned in both packages.
- Ask 2 (receipt vs marker column weighed, receipt chosen with no new key): done in the PR body.
- Ask 3 (`externalId` stable under the rename): the plan pin covers it, and the verb pin covers it with ablation red. The rename skip for `seed` items in the verb keeps the free-text rewrite out of record values.
- Ask 4 (load order): pinned. The child dataset is listed first and `multiPass` resolves `account`; the dogfood activity's `account` resolves too.
- Ask 5 (409 re-run): pinned at both layers with no new writes.
- Ask 6 (file blobs and quotas): the dev's premise correction is right. `SeedSchema.files` exists (`seed.zod.ts:343`), and the receipt keeps it (the body is `{ ...dataset, object }`, filtered to `SeedSchema.shape` on read). But no case in the diff copies a dataset that carries `files`, so the changeset's "a dataset's `files` map is loaded as on a managed install too" is unpinned. → should-fix S5. Quotas are stated honestly as framework none and cloud unverified.

**Correct by reading.**
- The plan puts `seed` items after every other item, so each object's table exists first.
- A `seed` item refused by the save door rolls the whole copy back (pinned, `failedItem`).
- The `isRuntimeCreatable('seed')` finding is on key `data` (pinned, ablated).
- An unreadable receipt is never folded into "no sample data": the install answers `skipped` with its reason, and the purge answers 503 with nothing deleted (pinned, ablated).
- The managed purge path is unchanged apart from moving into `purgeSeedDatasets` with a non-null entry. The ledger flag write is now guarded on `entry`.

**(e) `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`.** This is a legitimate pin update, and no gate is weakened. The file's own header calls it the RETAINED **coverage** ledger, which may only grow; the debt ledger is `engine-double-contract.baseline.json`, which is not in the diff. The edit only adds two rows, `update` and `delete` for `marketplace-install-local-install-modes.test.ts`, each `pinned: 1`, and removes none. They match the new harness, whose `update`/`delete` now call `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` / `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`. That is the dev's fix for the gate's first red. Nothing is loosened. The family that runs this gate on CI (Lint · CI, release & engine gates) is NOT MEASURED on this head.

### ② Semver level

**(d)** The changeset is `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': patch` and `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`, with both declaration lines line-initial: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. **Level right.** Under AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist 3, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right too. Nothing a metadata author writes changes: `seed` is an existing type, `data` an existing key, and the switch lives in an HTTP door body, not in metadata. Neither moved package re-exports a new symbol.

**Clause-②:** `yes (widening)` is the right kind and arm. As written, the line is incomplete in both the PR body and the changeset: it names the install door's `seedSampleData` and the verb's `seedData`, but not the purge door's new accept set or that set's reach to every writable base (S1).

**Text vs diff.** The changeset matches the diff except in three places:
- "on a copy" understates the purge reach (S1).
- It does not say that a seedless writable base, including an unmanaged copy installed without `seedSampleData`, now answers 400 `NOTHING_TO_PURGE` ("This package declares no seed datasets.") where it answered 404. For a copy whose package does declare data, that message is misleading (nit N1).
- "a copied `seed` item … published later behaves as every environment `seed` item does" leaves out the after-purge re-insert (S3). Its files sentence is unpinned (S5).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none.
- **Premise correction: seeds carry file bytes.** Accepted. It is right against `seed.zod.ts`, and the claim amendment recorded it before build. The files load is unpinned (S5).
- **Premise correction: quotas.** Accepted as stated. Whether the hosted cloud enforces a record quota is unverified here. That belongs to the cloud#3626 deep-link owner, not to this repo. Escalated to the seat to carry onto that card.
- **Premise correction: the verb body lives in `protocol-package-commits.ts`.** Accepted. It is covered by the claim amendment's file surface.
- **Out-of-scope class a: `getMetaItems({ type: 'seed' })` lists no stored seed item.** Real, and the PR works around it by reading by name. The report gives dedupe words but the finding is not filed. Escalated: the seat files it (or dedupes it) before landing. Each purge of a copy depends on the by-name workaround, and a fix to the list must not break it.
- **Out-of-scope: the stale `data: 'door'` comment in `packages/spec/src/kernel/unmanaged-install.ts`.** Right not to touch, since it is spec text. Escalated to the spec seat as noted. It should be filed, not left as "noted".
- **Out-of-scope: uninstalling a copy removes the receipt and leaves the rows, and `withSampleData` / reseed do not cover a copy.** It is stated in the PR's Acceptance notes. Once the hosted deep link (cloud#3626) turns the switch on, users hit this through the hosted flow. Escalated: the seat files a follow-up card (should-fix S6). There is also no door that re-loads a copy's receipt after a `seed-receipt-unread` or `seed-error` install, since a re-run answers 409. That belongs in the same card.

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix:**
- **S1.** Name the purge door's widening in the `Clause-②` line of the PR body and the changeset. Either narrow the non-ledger branch to unmanaged copies, or state in writing that it reaches every installed writable base's `seed` items, Studio-authored bases included.
- **S2.** Make the save pin discriminating: run `saveMetaItem({ mode: 'publish' })` on a receipt item with the rows absent (the post-purge state), and assert 0 inserts.
- **S3.** State in the changeset and PR body that a purge leaves the receipt, and that publishing a receipt item afterwards loads its rows again under the publish path's owner rule, not the installer's. Pin it, or state that it is left unpinned.
- **S4.** Add the card's required consequence sentence: per-role answers in the customer's environment differ from the gallery's recorded per-persona transcripts, and the gallery proves per-role behaviour through those transcripts, not live.
- **S5.** Pin the copy of a dataset that carries `files` (a `sys_file` minted per row), or soften the changeset's files sentence to what is measured.
- **S6.** File the follow-ups: the `getMetaItems` seed listing, the stale spec comment, and uninstall/reseed/count for a copy.

**Nits:**
- **N1.** The purge of a copy installed without `seedSampleData` answers 400 "declares no seed datasets" for a package that may declare some.
- **N2.** A receipt item a person edited into something that is not a dataset makes every later purge answer 503 "Retry once the metadata store answers", which is the wrong prescription for that cause.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-b11gkm`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5pXkgNXVpCn2GZDjyy`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `86246c5b01e81a07ff8d0acd5dddc082ae27b932`
Local-runs: none

Round 2, a delta review against the round-1 record (comment 6718084382, head `da697f3f`). Inputs read: card #30808 (body and every comment; nothing new since round 1), PR #31398 as it stands on GitHub (body and file list, 13 files), the net diff against `main`, the delta `da697f3f..86246c5b` (commits `7c35c693`, `97808a91`, the merge `79be15ea`, and `86246c5b`), and the check-runs on this head. The dev's proposed round-2 body (`30808-pr-body-r2.md`) and gates file were read as the dev's account, not as evidence. Code outside the diff was read to judge the diff, not reviewed: the protocol's `deletePackage` and `runUninstallCleanups`, the runtime's `DELETE /packages/:id` dispatcher, `purgeSeedRows`, and the cloud-connection route ledger.

### ① Derived judgments

**Gate verdicts on this head (check-runs).** Green: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Flag docs, Test UI, Plan Test Core shards, filter, Auto Label. **NOT MEASURED (in progress at review time):** Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Lint · CI, release & engine gates (the family that carries `check:engine-double-contract`), Lint · ESLint, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI, and Type Check · workspace, consumer gates, debt ledger and source gates. **Dogfood Regression Gate** reads success, but its shards are `skipped` off the merge queue, as in round 1. The dogfood file is NOT MEASURED in CI on this head; it is measured in the queue. This PASS judges the code. Landing waits for every NOT MEASURED family.

**The merge.** `79be15ea` brings in `origin/main` at `3a0aa915` (#31388) with no hand resolution: the combined diff of the door file is empty. #31388 changes only the cloud-fetched branch's register catch (`refusesBareNameHeldElsewhere`). It does not touch the unmanaged path, the purge or the uninstall, and it is not in this PR's net diff. Nothing new on the contract face comes from the merge.

**S1 — the purge door's reach. Closed in code. The declaration is closed in the changeset and still open in the PR body.**
- Code. `unmanagedCopyPurgeDatasets` now reads the door's own record (`UnmanagedCopyRecord`, one JSON file per base under `unmanaged-copies/` in the ledger directory) before anything else. With no record it answers `null`, which the handler turns into 404. With a record it then requires the base to be installed and writable, as before. A recorded copy made without `seedSampleData` answers `notSeeded`. The record is written in `installUnmanaged` right after the verb returns and before any row is loaded. The only other writer is the uninstall cleanup that removes it. No HTTP input names a record, and `isRecordEntry` rejects a file whose `baseId` differs from the id asked, so a filename sanitizer collision reads as a failure and never as a reach. The pins are discriminating by reading. A Studio-authored, installed, writable base with an active `seed` item naming an existing row answers 404 with no write. Before this patch that case reached the delete. A copy with its record removed answers 404. The managed path (`ledger.has`) is unchanged.
- *Can the purge reach a base that is not a recorded copy?* Not by id. By row, a recorded copy's receipt can name another base's object in a dataset's `object`. A `manage_metadata` holder can edit a copy's `seed` item, and `purgeSeedRows` deletes under `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT` without checking that the object is the base's own. But the same capability can already install an inline managed manifest whose datasets name any object, and purge that. So this reach is not new, and it is no finding.
- *A stale record.* The record says only that the door once copied *this id*. It does not bind to the base instance. A record outlives its base in four cases: the base is removed by a protocol without `registerUninstallCleanup`; the cleanup's `rmSync` fails, which is reported as `success: false` on the answer but leaves the file; the base is removed on a runtime whose ledger directory is not this one (another replica, or a run without the door composed); or an uninstall lands between the verb's return and the record write. In each case the purge answers 404 while no base holds the id. But a later base under the same id is reached. The PR body itself names the likeliest one: `-copy` is also the Studio duplicate's default id. The door's own docblock ("the purge still answers 404 for a record whose base is gone") stops one step short of that, and the changeset's "every other writable base, a Studio-authored one included, keeps the 404" is stated without the condition. → should-fix S7.
- *A record for an uninstalled base.* The base check runs after the record read, so the purge answers 404. The protocol's `deletePackage` runs every cleanup for any id it is asked about, partial failures included, and the import's own rollback goes through it too. So the normal path removes the record, and a partial uninstall fails closed (404).
- *A concurrent uninstall.* A purge that has passed the base check deletes only the rows its receipt named, in the objects the receipt named. Rows the uninstall leaves behind anyway, or engine errors counted in `errors`. No new reach.
- *An unreadable record.* The purge answers 503 with nothing deleted (pinned, and ablated per the dev's account). Two wording faults, below as N4.
- Declaration. The changeset's `Clause-②` line now names all three widenings: the install door's `seedSampleData`, the purge door now reaching a copy this door made (and that it answered 404 before), and the verb's `seedData`. That is right. **The PR body on GitHub is still the round-1 body**, and its `Clause-②` line names only two of them. The dev's proposed `30808-pr-body-r2.md` carries the right line but is not posted. → should-fix S8.

**S2 — the save pin. Closed.** The new case saves the receipt item with `saveMetaItem({ mode: 'publish' })` with every row of the dataset absent, the post-purge state, and asserts 0 inserts and an empty table. A save that applied the seed would insert both rows, so the pin discriminates.

**S3 — publish after purge. Closed in the changeset and pinned. The PR body is open (S8).** The changeset now says it: "Published after a purge, it loads its rows again under the publish rule, not the installer's: the publish names no person, so those rows carry no `owner_id` or `created_by`." It also says the purge leaves the receipt ("an uninstall removes the receipt"; "Published after a purge"). The new case drafts and publishes with no rows present and asserts `inserted: 2` with `organization_id: 'org_1'` and `owner_id`/`created_by` undefined.

**S4 — the persona consequence. Closed in the changeset. The PR body is open (S8).** The changeset now carries the card's required sentence: rows under different personas collapse to one owner, "so per-role answers in the customer's environment differ from the gallery's per-persona transcripts." That is the consequence the card's governing-rulings paragraph says to state.

**S5 — `files`. Closed.** The changeset no longer claims the bytes load on a copy: "loading those bytes on a copy is not exercised by a test here." Two new pins measure what the PR does implement. The verb keeps a dataset's `files` map in the receipt verbatim. `seedDatasetOfReceiptItem` keeps `files` (and every `SeedSchema` member) and drops an undeclared key.

**N1 — the message for a copy without sample data. Closed.** A recorded copy made without `seedSampleData` answers 400 `NOTHING_TO_PURGE` "No sample data was copied into '…': it was installed unmanaged without `seedSampleData`". The pin asserts the text and asserts that the old "declares no seed datasets" wording is absent. A copy whose receipt has since been emptied gets its own 400 sentence (`nothingToPurge`). The managed sentence is unchanged.

**New on this head: the cleanup outcome on every uninstall answer.** The door registers `install-local:unmanaged-copy-record` with the protocol's uninstall cleanups at `kernel:ready`. It runs on every uninstall of every package, not only of copies. Its outcome `{ name, success: true, removed: 0 }` now appears in:
- `data.cleanups` of `DELETE /marketplace/install-local/:id` (pinned by `86246c5b`);
- `cleanups` of the protocol's `deletePackage`, which `DELETE /packages/:id` serves as `persisted.cleanups`, and the `PACKAGE_DELETE_PARTIAL` 400's `details.cleanups`.
